title: Developer Experience Documentation Playbook: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Ops, and Canonical Fixes
author: Asha Patel
body:
Purpose
This playbook defines the standard structure, templates, operating procedures, and canonical fixes for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation at Redwood Inference. It covers SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs-site operating procedures (build/release/monitoring), and the top support issues plus canonical fixes we ship to customers and reference internally.

Scope
- All public and internal SDK guides (Python, JavaScript, Go, Java).
- Quickstarts and reference templates distributed via the docs site and the SDK repos.
- API examples (curl, REST, SDK-first snippets) used in the docs site and SDK READMEs.
- Docs site build, release, and monitoring procedures.
- Canonical fixes for top recurring developer support issues.

Ownership and SLAs
- Primary owner: DevEx docs team (eng-developer-experience).
- Secondary owners: SDK maintainers, API product manager.
- Review SLO: docs must have a technical review within 5 business days for security-sensitive changes, 10 business days otherwise.
- Production docs site uptime SLO: 99.9% monthly (tracked in eng-platform dashboards).

Document Types & When to Use Them
1) SDK Guide (long-form) — Use when documenting API surface, lifecycle of objects, advanced features (streaming, function calling, batching).
2) Quickstart — Minimal working example for first-time users, < 10 minute setup.
3) Template — Copy/paste project scaffolds, CI snippets, k8s manifests, and policy examples.
4) API Example Snippets — Short, single-purpose examples shown inline next to the API docs.
5) Runbook / Site Ops Page — Procedures for releasing the docs site, rollback, and incident recovery.

Required Metadata for Every Doc
- title, space, author, owner_team, status, created_at, last_updated (already tracked in our Confluence metadata standard).
- tags/labels (0-8) and reviewers recommended.

Standard Page Structure (SDK Guide)
- Title and one-line summary
- Short intro: who this doc is for and what it covers
- Prerequisites: SDK versions, auth, account prerequisites
- Quickstart (1-3 commands)
- Concepts: explain objects, flows, and cost/latency tradeoffs
- Examples: minimal, advanced, troubleshooting
- API reference / link to model catalog
- Compatibility and upgrade notes
- Tests and linting for examples (how to run locally)
- Change history and related pages

Quickstart Template (example)
- Purpose: onboard user in <10 minutes
- Assumptions: Python 3.10+, pip, Redwood API key

Commands:
```
# create and activate venv
python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate
pip install redwood-inference-sdk
```
Python quickstart snippet:
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
resp = client.chat.create(model="redwood-1.0", messages=[{"role": "system", "content": "You are helpful."}, {"role": "user", "content": "Give me a haiku about latency."}])
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)
```
JavaScript quickstart snippet:
```
import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY })
const resp = await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-1.0', messages: [{ role: 'user', content: 'Summarize the 12-factor app.' }] })
console.log(resp.choices[0].message.content)
```
Each quickstart must include: environment variables, minimal auth example, expected output, and a link to the full guide.

API Example Guidelines
- Keep examples <= 12 lines.
- Provide at least: curl, Python SDK, JavaScript SDK.
- Use realistic payloads (typical token lengths) and include headers for tracing (X-Request-ID).
- For streaming examples show both the event stream and a non-streaming version.
- Example naming convention: example-<feature>-<lang> (e.g., example-streaming-python).

Example: curl + Python + JS for text generation
```
# curl
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Explain continuous batching."}] }'
```
Python (sync):
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
c = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
print(c.chat.create(model='redwood-1.0', messages=[{'role':'user','content':'Explain continuous batching.'}]).choices[0].message.content)
```
JS (streaming outline):
```
const stream = client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-1.0', messages: [...] })
for await (const chunk of stream) { process.stdout.write(chunk.delta) }
```

Docs Site Operating Procedures (build, release, rollback)
1) Branching strategy
  - docs-main: canonical published branch.
  - feature/<owner>-short-desc: for doc changes.
  - hotfix/<ticket-id>: for urgent fixes that must ship in <24h.
2) Pull request checklist (required before merge):
  - [ ] Doc owner listed in PR title/body
  - [ ] Technical review completed (reviewers listed)
  - [ ] Code samples execute successfully (CI: examples/test.sh)
  - [ ] Accessibility checked (alt text for images, headings order)
  - [ ] Labels added: area, language, severity (if applicable)
3) CI Build and Lint
  - Run docs-lint and examples tests. Docs CI will fail if: broken links, invalid frontmatter, or example tests fail.
4) Release process
  - Merge to docs-main triggers Netlify build (or docs-prod pipeline).
  - Post-merge: verify build status in CI and smoke test 3 sample pages (home, SDK quickstart, API reference).
  - Deploy verification window: 15 minutes; if critical errors appear, rollback to previous build and open hotfix.
5) Rollback
  - Revert merge commit or re-deploy previous successful build via Netlify/CI dashboard. Notify #devex and #eng-ops.

Monitoring and KPIs
- Page availability (monitoring ping every 1m), build success rate, time-to-merge for doc PRs, average time to close doc support tickets.
- Target KPIs: build success rate > 98%, average doc PR time-to-merge < 7 days, doc support ticket mean time to resolution < 48 hours.

Localization and Versioning
- Primary language: English. Secondary languages (customer-driven) follow a gated process: translate, review by native speaker reviewer, then publish behind the i18n switch.
- Versioning: SDK APIs should include compatibility notes and migration guides when breaking changes land. Tag docs with the SDK major version (e.g., v1.x).

Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes (current list, owner: DevEx + SDK teams)
1) Auth errors: invalid API key / 401
   - Symptom: rapid 401s in logs, customers see "Unauthorized".
   - Canonical fix: show explicit quickstart to set REDWOOD_API_KEY, add auth-check endpoint snippet, and add troubleshooting section recommending curl -I to inspect headers.
   - Detection: support ticket template includes sample request with Authorization header.
2) Streaming examples time out / truncated messages
   - Symptom: partial payloads, client-side timeouts.
   - Canonical fix: include streaming heartbeat example, increase client read timeout, and recommend using official SDK stream helpers.
3) Model mismatch / 400 invalid parameters
   - Symptom: 400 with "unsupported-model" or "max_sequence_length" errors.
   - Canonical fix: update examples to explicitly set model and max_tokens; link to model catalog and compat table.
4) SDK installation issues (wheel vs. source, mac M1)
   - Symptom: build errors on pip install or native compilation issues on M1.
   - Canonical fix: provide prebuilt wheels in PyPI tags and Homebrew instruction; include troubleshooting: upgrade pip, install build tools.
5) Rate limit confusion (429)
   - Symptom: users receive 429s unexpectedly during burst tests.
   - Canonical fix: document per-project rate limits, show retry-after header handling example, provide client-side exponential backoff snippet.
6) Incorrect streaming ++ function-calling ordering (JS SDK)
   - Symptom: function-calling payloads arriving out of order in webhooks.
   - Canonical fix: standardize on sequence ID in messages and show canonical server-side handler example.
7) Tokenization surprises / cost higher than expected
   - Symptom: reported token usage higher than docs examples.
   - Canonical fix: include tokenization examples and recommended tokenizer usage snippets; provide guidance for prompt engineering to reduce tokens.
8) Examples that rely on deprecated endpoints
   - Symptom: 404s after API upgrades.
   - Canonical fix: nightly lint job flags deprecated endpoints; remove/replace examples and add deprecation notice in CHANGELOG.
9) Broken links after site restructure
   - Symptom: 404s in search queries, user complaints.
   - Canonical fix: keep redirect map in repo (redirects.csv) and CI check for changed slugs that lack redirects.
10) Misleading error messages for quota/billing issues
   - Symptom: errors attribute generic "request failed" without billing context.
   - Canonical fix: update API error docs to include billing-specific codes and a triage flow (check project usage, invoicing, contact support).

Each canonical fix must be codified as: doc change + example fix in SDK repo + test that reproduces the issue. Owner must add a related page and a support KB entry.

Process to Add a New Quickstart or Canonical Fix
1) Create feature/<owner>-short-desc branch.
2) Add page under quickstarts-and-templates with the standard frontmatter and the quickstart skeleton.
3) Add runnable examples under /examples/<language>/<quickstart-name> in the repo and a CI job that runs them.
4) Request review from SDK maintainers and add reviewers to the PR.
5) After merge, add redirect and update the related_pages field in metadata.
6) Close loop: add an entry in the support KB and tag the fix with the support ticket IDs.

Canonical Fix Example (Rate Limit Handling - Python)
```
from redwood import RedwoodClient
c = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
for i in range(10):
  try:
    resp = c.chat.create(model='redwood-1.0', messages=[{'role':'user','content':'test'}])
    break
  except RedwoodRateLimitError as e:
    sleep_time = min(60, (2 ** i) * 0.5)
    time.sleep(sleep_time)
```

Maintenance Cadence
- Quarterly review: update quickstarts and SDK guides for any major API or model changes.
- Weekly: triage doc-related support tickets and prioritize hotfixes.
- Nightly: CI checks for broken links and example tests.

Useful repo locations and contact points
- DevEx docs repo: github.com/redwood-inference/devex-docs (examples/ and site/)
- SDK repos: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python, sdk-js, sdk-go
- Slack channels: #devex, #devex-review, #eng-ops, #support
- Pager rotation for docs site outages: eng-platform on-call (see eng-platform/roster)

FAQ (short)
Q: Who signs off on customer-facing Quickstarts?
A: DevEx content owner + SDK maintainer must both approve.
Q: How do we ensure examples stay runnable?
A: All examples live in the examples/ folder and are executed by CI tests on pull request.

Appendix: Quick metadata checklist for authors
- Title: concise and searchable
- One-line summary: 10-15 words
- Audience: developer type (frontend/backend/platform)
- Languages supported: list (Python, JS, Go)
- Example test command: examples/test.sh --quickstart <name>
- Owner and reviewers: add to page metadata
